clone_manifest_note: One entry per clone of each sweep; instance ids are positional (clone-<role>-<arch>-<index>).
concordance_note: One value per suite, scored against Ensembl VEP 116.2's archived output (perl_reference names the sets): every clone of both architectures of the concordance sweep reported the same raw and adjusted F1 and the same tuple counts (F1 is deterministic per binary and architecture-independent). The README's "Current release" tables render these values from this record at nine decimal places, recomputed from the tuple counts. Adjusted F1 is 1.0 on every suite. Tuple counts move against v0.3.2 on s01, s02, s07, s08; the movement is in this record, previous_release_concordance beside concordance per cell and per file for the structural-variant cells, and in the README's "Current release" tables, which render the re-scored rows beneath this version's. The paired run of the previous release (previous_release_concordance, the same day, the same clones' protocol, the same Ensembl VEP 116.2 reference) is the comparison basis: raw F1 and tuple counts are held not below it on every suite.
dataset_inventory_sha256_note: One value per sweep, identical across its clones of both architectures (each clone entry carries its own). The concordance sweep's clones also synced the archived Perl ground truth the comparator reads, so its inventory covers more files than the wall-time sweep's.

field_agreement.note: compare_vep_fields.py on every concordance clone of the release (v0.4.0 candidate 72ce119b, 2 + 2 clones) and of the previous release (v0.3.2 re-scored, 1 + 1 clones), the same day, both against the Ensembl VEP 116.2 reference set: per suite the key totals and, per output column, the rows compared (both engines wrote the key), equal and differing. Only s01 and s02 are field-compared in this fleet: the structural-variant cells (s07 to s10) have no per-column comparator. columns_differing_from_previous lists every (suite, column) whose compared/equal/differ counts differ from the previous release's paired clone; a listed column whose compared count rose with differ 0 means the released version agrees with Ensembl VEP on more tuples than the previous release did, and an empty list means it agrees column for column exactly where the previous release did.

harness_skip_fields_note: The per-column field comparator (compare_vep_fields.py) ran on every concordance clone of both releases; field_agreement summarises the released version's per-suite, per-column agreement and names every column whose agreement differs from the previous release's.
methodology_note: r8gd.8xlarge (ARM Graviton4) and r8id.8xlarge (Intel x86_64), 32 vCPU / 256 GiB / local NVMe instance store, spec-matched; 20 fresh clones per architecture booting the stock AL2023 base image, each syncing the dataset to local NVMe. The wall-time sweep runs scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh --walltime-only (--fork 16, sites-only inputs): one cold-cache warmup (discarded) and one timed measurement per cell, then self-terminates; median and P5/P95 across the clones per cell (Weibull, R type 6). The concordance sweep runs the same script without --walltime-only, so each clone also computes the 6-cell concordance report against the archived Perl ground truth; its wall times are not used, because the comparator running between suites perturbs the timed run that follows a warmup on the largest output.
per_cell_aggregates_note: Wall time per (arch, suite) over the completed clones of the wall-time sweep (median and quantiles by the Weibull estimator, R type 6); each of those clones' entry under clones carries the per-suite wall time it reported (wall_time_sec), so every aggregate re-derives from this record. The README's "Current release" table renders these values.

population_concordance.note: Whole-genome concordance of the released binary against Ensembl VEP 116.2's archived output on four population datasets, one clone per chromosome shard (the pool arch's), the same comparator, cache and reference FASTA as the genome-wide ClinVar and structural-variant cells. A variant is one VCF record; a tuple is one output row reduced to (Location, Allele, Feature, Feature_type, Consequence set); F1 is pooled by summed counts (micro-F1), raw with nothing set aside and adjusted with the documented divergence classes set aside. Wall time per shard is carried in the fleet archive as information only.

public_build_inputs_note: Git object ids of the build inputs at source_commit (crates tree, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, .cargo/config.toml), re-derived by the build host from the extracted source and recorded with the binary; a tag whose inputs equal these carries the code that was measured.
rustc_note: The compiler of the measured binaries, read from the build markers of both architectures; it is the toolchain the release workflow pins, so the release assets are builds of the same source, lockfile and compiler, identified by their own digests in SHA256SUMS.

same_day_control.note: Both binaries under the release protocol on the same day (--walltime-only, the discarded warmup's output flushed and deleted before the timed run), on the same instance types and images: the released version (20 + 20 clones) and the previous release (3 + 3 clones) agree within 2.8% in median wall time on 8 of 8 cells and within 1.1% in median user CPU time on every cell above 60 CPU-seconds.

scope: vep-rs alone: the released version's concordance on the cells s01, s02, s07, s08, s09, s10 against Ensembl VEP 116.2's archived output (perl_reference names the sets) and its own wall times on both architectures, stated in the README beside the paper's figures, which do not change. Perl VEP and fastVEP are not re-measured here, and no ratio against the paper's medians is stated: the release protocol deletes the discarded warmup's output before the timed run and the paper's did not. The same-day control below is the comparison the README cites.
sites_only_note: Every timed input is sites-only; s09 and s10 are pointer suites into the per-file structural-variant results of s07 and s08.
warmup_output_discarded_note: Before each timed run the harness flushes and deletes the discarded warmup's output (scripts/concordance/run_clone_measurement.sh, discard_warmup_output), so the timed run starts with the memory the warmup had.
